title: Gentle deploy scratchpad — boarding cohorts and tether heuristics
content:
Purpose:
Quick, personal playbook for a low-noise gradual deploy pattern Im trialing: "quiet boarding". Focus is incremental client onboarding (tether cohorts), short observation windows, and an explicit throttle leash so we can pause without full rollback.

Overview / goal:
- Get model/service changes to production while minimizing user-visible surprise.
- Prefer containment (stop forward traffic to new variant) over full rollback when we see regressions.
- Keep incident blast radius small by using short-lived cohorts that can be unlinked quickly.

Key concepts (informal):
- Boarding cohort: a small cohort of clients (1–3% each) that are routed to the new variant for a short probe window (5–20 min). Usually anchored to stable tenants or internal test clients first.
- Tether: a circuit that keeps a cohort pinned while we validate; can be cut (untether) to divert traffic immediately without flipping whole-route pins.
- Throttle leash: a soft cap on per-client QPS/throughput for cohort traffic so we avoid consuming capacity that affects baseline.
- Gatekeeper probe: a quick smoke and correctness run across a handful of scripted prompts or evals (local conformance) run at cohort spin-up.

Deployment plan (example sequence):
1) Preflight (T-24h to T-10m)
   - Publish rollout note in #deploys with planned windows + link to this doc and RLSD-312.
   - Confirm required dashboards are pinned: routing traffic split, p99 latency, error rate, token cost delta, per-tenant error spikes.
   - Ensure fastback runbook is in top of signal: who is oncall, who can cut the tether, who owns rollback PRs.
   - Warm KV/cache priming plan for any model weight changes (if applicable).

2) Spin internal cohort (T+0) — 1% traffic to internal-demo tenants
   - Duration: 10 min stable window. Run Gatekeeper probe (scripts/gatekeeper/quick-smoke.sh).
   - Watchpoints: generation correctness quick-check, p95/p99 latency, rejected-token ratio, any auth/error codes.
   - If green -> proceed. If blip -> untether internal cohort, annotate and re-run after fix.

3) Anchor cohort — 3% (mix of low-risk customer tenants)
   - Duration: 15–30 min. Add throttle leash at 0.7x normal QPS per-client.
   - Run a small matrix of eval prompts (happy path + edge cases).
   - Check long-tail cost estimates (token delta * sample traffic).

4) Gradual ramp steps: 3% -> 10% -> 25%
   - Each step is ~30–45 min observation window.
   - Rules at each step:
       * If p99 > baseline + 80ms AND error rate increased > 50% relative -> cut tether for last cohort and drop to previous step.
       * If any single tenant experiences > 5% increase in 5xx errors -> untether that tenant (client-level cut) and alert owner.
       * If model output regression (manually confirmed) -> stop and escalate.

Fastback (preferred over full rollback):
- Action: cut tether(s) for the last n cohorts (by cohort id), divert to baseline model/variant.
- Why: isolates the failure and avoids forcing all clients back. Gives time to hotfix without major user disruption.
- Required: automated scripts to cut tether by cohort id (ops/runbooks/cut-tether.sh) and dashboard to confirm cut.

Key metrics to instrument / queries to run in the window:
- p50, p95, p99 latency (generator + roundtrip) — compare to baseline percentiles.
- Token-rate & token-cost delta per-minute.
- Per-tenant 5xx and 4xx rate (spikes per tenant).
- User-facing regression rate: rejects / hallucination markers flagged by quick evals.
- SLO burn rate (if we have token-cost-pv SLOs).
- Queue/backpressure signals on serving runtime: request queue depth per GPU, mem pressure.

Safety thresholds (early abort):
- Any tenant sees >5x baseline 5xx for 5 consecutive mins -> immediate untether for that tenant + pager.
- Global p99 > baseline + 200ms for 10+ mins -> stop ramp, untether last cohorts.
- Cost: if token-cost growth projects > +30% vs evening baseline for sustained 30 min -> pause and review.

Preflight checks (ticklist):
- [ ] Gatekeeper scripts present and smoke passes locally
- [ ] Canary cohort creation script works and returns cohort ids
- [ ] Cut-tether script tested from staging (dry-run)
- [ ] Dashboard links posted to #deploys and bookmarks set
- [ ] Oncall + product owner aware of windows and watchlist tenants

Operational notes and tips (personal):
- Keep cohorts small and anchored to low-variance tenants first. Avoid selecting heavy-burst customers for initial cohorts.
- Use feature-flags to toggle qualitative changes (e.g., prompt tweaks) separate from model binary flips. Easier to revert.
- If you see transient latency spikes aligned with big cloud events, lean toward waiting an extra window (dont overreact to noisy infra).
- Annotate every untether action in the rollout note with reason + metric snapshot. Helps postmortem and acceptance.

Questions / open items:
- Need an easy UI path for solutions engineers to request temporary tether cuts for a tenant (self-service). Who owns that UI?
- Can we add a per-cohort synthetic eval that runs every 2 minutes and reports a single pass/fail flag to the dashboard? (would reduce manual checks)
- Should throttle leash be absolute QPS or percent of historical tenant QPS? Prefer percent but need per-tenant profile data accessible quickly.

After-action notes (template to copy into RLSD-312 if something happens):
- Time window, cohorts spun, who untethered (if any), immediate metric deltas, root-cause hypothesis, next steps.

Quick commands (ops shortcuts):
- Create cohort: scripts/rollout/create_cohort --variant vX --pct 3 --owners samir
- Cut tether: scripts/rollout/cut_tether --cohort COHORT_ID --reason "spike-5xx"
- Rollback variant: scripts/rollout/flip_variant --route main --variant baseline --force

Random ideas to experiment with next time:
- Staggered warmup within a cohort (start at 10% of cohort traffic for 5m then go to 100%) to reduce initial shock.
- Synthetic "canary clients" that simulate typical tenant behavior and emit ground-truth signals.
- One-button snapshot: capture current traces + token-cost projection + top-10 tenants by delta and attach to rollout note.

Notes to self: keep this lightweight. This doc is my working ground; prune and move stable procedures to Confluence once tuned.
